caffeine can extract mutagenic ethylium (Et) cations from DNA and various cell lines and the efficiency of the extraction is cell type dependent.

caffeine is a potential antimutagent and its efficiency in removing the potential mutagen, ethidium (a DNA-binding dye), from synthetic DNA and whole cells is dependent on cell type.

the use of ultrafast spectroscopy and other biophysical techniques for the investigation of molecular mechanisms of mutagenesis and the development of novel antimutagenic therapeutics.
the study of the interaction of caffeine with DNA, its complex with Et, and its ability to extract Et from whole cells.

caffeine, a widely used drug, has the ability to dissociate mutagenic ethylidium cation from DNA and cell nuclei, and thus can potentially be used to prevent the mutagenic action of Et in vivo.
caffeine can act as an efficient antimutagenic agent in the human body.
caffeine, in the concentration range of 1-2 mM, is an effective antimutagenic agent, and it is capable of removing Et from DNA as well as from various cell nuclei.

caffeine is a very effective and versatile antimutagenic agent.

caffeine, a widely used stimulant, has a potential to be a therapeutic agent for cancer and other DNA-related diseases.
